extracted.intended_audience: public water systems (PWS), State primacy agencies, water system operators, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_short: NPDWR compliance for public water systems
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards public water systems must follow under 40 CFR Part 141 (National Primary Drinking Water Regulations), including MCLs, monitoring, treatment techniques, reporting, public notification, and special rules (e.g., lead/copper, PFAS, Cryptosporidium).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability (§ 141.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: “This part establishes primary drinking water regulations pursuant to section 1412 of the Public Health Service Act, as amended by the Safe Drinking Water Act ... and related regulations applicable to public water systems.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope: Part 141 contains national primary drinking water regulations applicable to public water systems; use as the controlling regulatory authority for compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined terms and numeric action levels (selected definitions in § 141.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains critical definitions used throughout the part, including: Action level (for subpart I only: lead action level 0.010 mg/L and copper action level 1.3 mg/L); community water system; finished water; CT/CTcalc; best available technology (BAT); compliance cycle/period; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many compliance rules depend on these definitions (e.g., what constitutes an action level, how CT is calculated, who is a community water system). Treat the definitions as normative for interpreting monitoring, treatment, and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCLs) and Maximum Residual Disinfectant Levels (MRDLs) (§§ 141.11, 141.13, 141.61-141.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes MCLs for inorganic, organic, microbiological contaminants, disinfection byproducts, and radionuclides, and MRDLs for disinfectants; effective dates and applicability specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with MCLs/MRDLs is determined by specified monitoring and averaging rules in later sections; some contaminants have special effective dates and monitoring start dates by system size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and analytical requirements (Subpart C: §§ 141.21–141.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes coliform sampling (§141.21), turbidity sampling and analytical requirements (§141.22), inorganic chemical sampling (§141.23), organic chemical sampling (§141.24), radioactivity analytical methods (§141.25), monitoring frequency and compliance for radionuclides (§141.26), alternate analytical techniques (§141.27), certified laboratories (§141.28), and monitoring of consecutive systems (§141.29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies sampling schedules, analytical methods, certification requirements for labs, monitoring frequencies, and special rules for consecutive (downstream) systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements (§ 141.31) and Record maintenance (§ 141.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report monitoring results and other required information to the State in specified timeframes and retain records as required by the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting timelines, content, and record retention obligations vary by subpart; systems must follow §141.31 and §141.33 when compiling initial and compliance monitoring data and public-notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring requirements for unregulated contaminants (§ 141.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets monitoring requirements for unregulated contaminants (e.g., UCMR-type monitoring) including who must monitor and sampling design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to collect occurrence data for future regulatory determinations; follow specified schedules and analytical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special monitoring for sodium (§ 141.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes special monitoring for sodium where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may require sodium monitoring under specified conditions and use results to inform public information/health guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special monitoring for corrosivity characteristics (§ 141.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires monitoring for water corrosivity characteristics when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrosivity monitoring supports lead/copper control decisions and treatment/mitigation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum Contaminant Level Goals (MCLGs) and MRDLGs (§§ 141.50–141.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets non-enforceable health goals (MCLGs) and MRDLGs for organic, inorganic, microbiological contaminants, disinfection byproducts, disinfectants, and radionuclides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MCLGs/MRDLGs are health-based goals that inform MCL/MRDL setting but are not themselves enforceable limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration and Disinfection general requirements (§§ 141.70–141.76)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements for filtration and disinfection, criteria for avoiding filtration, disinfection requirements, filtration requirements, analytical and monitoring requirements, reporting/recordkeeping, and recycle provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when filtration is required or may be avoided, minimum disinfection/contact-time calculations (CT), turbidity and filter performance monitoring, and associated reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and Copper control framework (Subpart I: §§ 141.80–141.93)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart I provides: general requirements and action level (§141.80), applicability of corrosion control treatment steps (§141.81), description of corrosion control treatment requirements (§141.82), source water treatment requirements (§141.83), service line inventory and replacement requirements (§141.84), public education and supplemental monitoring/mitigation (§141.85), monitoring requirements for lead and copper in tap water (§141.86), monitoring for water quality parameters (§141.87), monitoring for lead and copper in source water (§141.88), analytical methods (§141.89), reporting (§141.90), recordkeeping (§141.91), monitoring for lead in schools and childcare (§141.92), small water system compliance flexibility (§141.93).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key numeric action level values: lead 0.010 mg/L and copper 1.3 mg/L. Contains detailed procedures for corrosion control evaluation, treatment triggers, service line inventories, replacement schedules, public education content, and monitoring/analytical protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-centralized treatment devices (§§ 141.100–141.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedures for public water systems using point-of-entry devices (§141.100) and use of bottled water (§141.101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets when and how non-centralized devices may be used, and regulatory limits/conditions for bottled water substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment techniques (§§ 141.110–141.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: General treatment technique requirements (§141.110) and specific treatment techniques for acrylamide and epichlorohydrin (§141.111).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an MCL cannot be established, a treatment technique (process-based requirement) may be required; this subpart sets the operational/monitoring expectations for such techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfectant Residuals, Disinfection Byproducts, and Precursors (Subpart L: §§ 141.130–141.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements (§141.130), analytical requirements (§141.131), monitoring (§141.132), compliance (§141.133), reporting and recordkeeping (§141.134), and a treatment technique for control of DBP precursors (§141.135).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how systems measure disinfectant residuals and DBPs, monitoring frequency, compliance calculations, and precursor control actions to reduce DBP formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Reports (Subpart O: §§ 141.151–141.156)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose/applicability (§141.151), compliance dates (§141.152), content of the reports (§141.153), required additional health information (§141.154), report delivery/reporting/recordkeeping (§141.155), and summary of report contents (§141.156).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines required CCR content and delivery methods to inform customers about water quality, violations, and health information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Filtration and Disinfection for large systems (Subpart P: §§ 141.170–141.175)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements (§141.170), criteria for avoiding filtration (§141.171), disinfection profiling and benchmarking (§141.172), filtration (§141.173), filtration sampling requirements (§141.174), and reporting/recordkeeping (§141.175) for systems serving 10,000 or more people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lays out additional, strengthened requirements for large systems including disinfection profiling/benchmarking, sampling, and filtration performance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notification of Drinking Water Violations (Subpart Q: §§ 141.201–141.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: General public notification requirements (§141.201); Tier 1 (§141.202), Tier 2 (§141.203), Tier 3 (§141.204) public notice form, manner, and frequency; content of the public notice (§141.205); notice to new billing units/customers (§141.206); special notices (§§141.207–141.211). Appendices provide violations requiring notice and standard health effects language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when and how systems must notify the public of violations or significant situations, with tiered notice forms, timelines, and required content, including appended model language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground Water Rule (Subpart S: §§ 141.400–141.405)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements/applicability (§141.400), sanitary surveys for ground water systems (§141.401), ground water source microbial monitoring and analytical methods (§141.402), treatment technique requirements (§141.403), treatment technique violations (§141.404), and reporting/recordkeeping (§141.405).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on microbial protection for ground water systems: sanitary surveys, source monitoring triggers, treatment obligations, and violation determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Filtration and Disinfection for systems <10,000 (Subpart T: §§ 141.500–141.571)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements (§141.500–141.503), finished water reservoirs (§141.510–141.511), additional watershed control for unfiltered systems (§141.520–141.522), disinfection profile development (§141.530–141.536), disinfection benchmark (§141.540–141.544), combined filter effluent and individual filter turbidity requirements (§141.550–141.564), and reporting/recordkeeping (§141.570–141.571).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to Subpart P but tailored for smaller systems; includes how to develop disinfection profiles and benchmarks, turbidity monitoring, and records/reporting required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Distribution System Evaluations (Subpart U: §§ 141.600–141.605)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements (§141.600), standard monitoring (§141.601), system-specific studies (§141.602), 40/30 certification (§141.603), very small system waivers (§141.604), and monitoring location recommendations (§141.605).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSEs determine where and how to monitor for disinfection byproducts to protect public health; includes options for studies and waivers for very small systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 Disinfection Byproducts Requirements (Subpart V: §§ 141.620–141.629)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements (§141.620), routine monitoring (§141.621), monitoring plan (§141.622), reduced monitoring (§141.623), additional requirements for consecutive systems (§141.624), conditions requiring increased monitoring (§141.625), operational evaluation levels (§141.626), and reporting/recordkeeping (§141.629).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes monitoring and operational response requirements to control DBPs including TTHM and HAA5 and criteria for reduced or increased monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Treatment for Cryptosporidium (Subpart W: §§ 141.700–141.723)
rubrics_metrics.description: General requirements (§141.700); source water monitoring (§141.701–141.707); disinfection profiling/benchmarking for significant disinfection changes (§141.708–141.709); treatment technique requirements (bin classification, additional Cryptosporidium treatment for filtered/unfiltered systems, schedules, storage facility requirements) (§141.710–141.714); microbial toolbox components (§141.715–141.720); reporting/recordkeeping (§141.721–141.722); and requirements to respond to significant deficiencies identified in EPA sanitary surveys (§141.723).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets source monitoring, classification and required treatment levels, approved toolbox options (filtration, inactivation, pre-treatment), and compliance schedules to reduce risk from Cryptosporidium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft Drinking Water Rule (Subpart X: §§ 141.800–141.810)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability and compliance date (§141.800), definitions (§141.801), coliform sampling plan and sampling (§141.802–141.803), aircraft water system operations and maintenance plan (§141.804), notification to passengers and crew (§141.805), reporting/recordkeeping (§141.806–141.807), audits/inspections (§141.808), supplemental treatment (§141.809), and violations (§141.810).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized requirements tailored to aircraft potable water systems addressing sampling, operations/maintenance plans, notification, and inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Total Coliform Rule (Subpart Y: §§ 141.851–141.861)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions (§141.851), analytical methods and laboratory certification (§141.852), general and system-specific routine monitoring requirements (§141.853–141.857), repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (§141.858), coliform treatment technique triggers and assessment requirements (§141.859), violations (§141.860), and reporting/recordkeeping (§141.861).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes monitoring based on system type and size, defines triggers for assessments and corrective actions, and details violation/reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) general requirements (Subpart Z: §§ 141.900–141.905)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart Z establishes general requirements (§141.900), analytical requirements (§141.901), monitoring requirements (§141.902), compliance requirements (§141.903), reporting and recordkeeping requirements (§141.904), and violations (§141.905) for PFAS contaminants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies MCLs and a Hazard Index for PFAS, prescribes sampling schedules (initial and compliance monitoring), use of trigger levels, and sets reporting/recordkeeping obligations specific to PFAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS initial monitoring and timing (§ 141.902(a), (b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial monitoring requirements: systems serving ≥75,000 begin monitoring 1 year after promulgation with MCL effective 2 years after promulgation; systems 10,000–75,000 begin within 3 years and MCL effective 4 years after promulgation. Initial monitoring must be completed by April 26, 2027 (per note).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial monitoring timing depends on system size; includes instructions on which results to include and state authority to delete obvious sampling errors (deleted results may create monitoring violations if not retaken).

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS compliance monitoring schedules and eligibility (§ 141.902(b)(2) and Table 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three compliance monitoring schedules: triennial, annual, quarterly. Eligibility for triennial includes all initial monitoring results below trigger levels or recent consecutive annual results below trigger levels; annual eligibility requires State determination of reliably and consistently below MCL after ≥4 consecutive quarterly samples; quarterly monitoring required if any initial sample meets/exceeds trigger levels or in other enumerated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If triggering occurs, systems must escalate to quarterly monitoring; the State may require confirmation samples and may increase monitoring frequency to detect variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS compliance determination method and averaging (§ 141.903(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For quarterly monitoring, compliance is based on a running annual average at each sampling point; for annual/triennial monitoring, detection at/above trigger or MCL triggers quarterly monitoring. Practical Quantitation Levels (PQLs) table specifies PQLs for PFAS analytes; sample results below PQL are treated as zero solely for running annual average calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed calculation procedures: averaging rules, treatment of confirmation samples, use of zeros for <PQL, and specific instructions for Hazard Index calculation for mixtures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS Hazard Index methodology (§ 141.903(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For Hazard Index PFAS, calculate hazard quotient for each analyte by dividing measured concentration by corresponding HBWC, sum quotients to obtain Hazard Index for each sampling event, average quarterly Hazard Indices to determine running annual average; exceedance rules require two or more analytes above PQL for a running annual average exceedance to be a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to compute and average the Hazard Index, how confirmation samples are handled, and trigger/escalation rules for Hazard Index exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS reporting and recordkeeping (§ 141.904)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to sample must report initial monitoring data and compliance monitoring data to the State per §141.31 and retain records per §141.33. Tables specify exact data to report for initial and compliance monitoring (sample locations, dates, concentrations, trigger/MCL exceedances, running annual averages, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting content varies by monitoring frequency; systems must report whether trigger levels or MCLs were met/exceeded and running annual averages when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS violations (§ 141.905)
rubrics_metrics.description: PFAS MCL violations are based on running annual averages; failure to collect required samples is a monitoring violation; failure to notify State after MCL violation and failure to submit monitoring data are reporting violations. Immediate out-of-compliance conditions exist if single-sample results are more than four times the MCL even before completing one year of quarterly sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that violations are per sampling point (a single sampling point violation makes the system in violation), describes when immediate violation is assessed, and clarifies how individual MCL and Hazard Index exceedances are compared and reported.
